_comment: #423: Hedault's own shop, indoors off the boulevard (user ruling 2026-08-10). Schema modelled on stationer.json -- small interior, perimeter is walls.segments so wall cells are NEVER also in `blocked`; `blocked` holds furniture only, each with a matching decor row. Biome + every sprite reused, zero biomes.json edits. No floor_layers: the brothers_parlor biome default is the plain interior board, which is neither the parlor's parquet nor the stationer's pale swatch -- a bespoke enchanter floor is a VISUAL-LOG art follow-up, not a blind region pick. THE POINT OF THE MAP: Hedault stands at (2,3) with THREE orthogonally-adjacent standable cells -- (1,3), (3,3), (2,4) -- every one of them walk-reachable from the shop door's landing at (6,7). The alleys placement he came from had none, which is issue #423.

segments._comment: The work-room partition, west arm: seals x7 at y1..y2 so the back pocket (x8..10, y1..2) has exactly ONE opening.
The partition's south arm. The gap it leaves at (8,3) is the work-room door -- the [Pick Lock] debut gate.

enchanter_work_room._comment: Descriptive registry (runtime never reads it): the work-room's TWO modes, contents identical. Mode 0 is the [Pick Lock] debut. Mode 1 is the virtuous path -- Hedault opens the door himself once the lady's commission is settled (hedault_enchanting's `work_room` arm), which is why it declares the non-skill `dialogue` gate rather than a skill union.

entities._comment: Round-trip pair with boulevard_enchanter_shop (invrisil_boulevard cell 22,1). Landing (6,7) is the open cell directly north of this door -- standable, off every prop, and the start of every walk in this map's QA legs.

#423: Hedault relocated from mercantile_alleys (0,6), where north and west were blocked, the bench sat east and the door cell sat south -- no standable cell could face him. Here (1,3)/(3,3)/(2,4) are all open and all reachable from (6,7). His talk_pool and `conversation` MOVED with him verbatim (not copied -- the alleys row is deleted in the same edit, so the anti-duplication gate stays satisfied).
talk_pool: Appraisal is free to watch and expensive to interrupt.
Do not touch the workbench. Do not touch the wares. Ideally, do not touch anything, including me.
Half this city's 'enchantments' are paint. The other half are apologies. I sell neither.
entities.observe: A severe man at a spotless corner bench, tools laid out at right angles. He looks at your gear before he looks at your face.

entities._comment: The enchanting bench fiction, brought in off the street. Sprite reuses the shipped temper_bench; a bespoke enchanter's bench is a VISUAL-LOG art follow-up.
entities.observe: Every tool on it lies square to the edge, and the one gap in the row is tool-shaped and clean. Whatever belongs there is in his hand.
Finished pieces, each on its own square of grey cloth, each with the cloth squared to the shelf edge. Nothing is priced where a customer can read it from the door.
Glass, and behind the glass a great deal of empty velvet. Four pieces are out, spaced far enough apart that you look at each one on its own.
Names down the left, work down the middle, and a third column of dates in a smaller hand. Half the dates have a second date beside them, later, and underlined.
Pieces somebody else enchanted, tagged and stacked for collection. The tags carry no verdict on them, only a name and an hour.

entities._comment: #423 THE [Pick Lock] DEBUT GATE, and the shape that keeps the two modes honest. `door_when` and `requires_skill` on ONE prop: interactions.gd checks door_when FIRST (line 93), so once `enchanter_work_room_opened` banks -- by the pick OR by Hedault's own arm -- this same interact becomes the transition, with no presence flip and therefore no same-map render ghost (the GH#104 class). Unmet + skill unknown falls through to use_skill's SKILL_UNKNOWN + locked_toast; unmet + skill known answers with skill_hint_toast (the explicit-Skill-use directive: interact never auto-casts).
entities.observe: A plain door in a plain partition, and a lock on it worth more than the door is. Three brass wards on the escutcheon, and the wear around the keyhole is all on one side.
entities.skill_hint_toast: Three wards and a shallow throw, and every scratch on the plate says the key goes in at an angle. Working it would take the picks and the patience.
entities.locked_toast: The lock is better than the door. You get as far as knowing that, and no further.

on_skill_use.toast: [Pick Lock] — Three wards, lifted one at a time, and the shallow throw goes over on the fourth breath. The door comes off the frame quietly, which is the only way it was ever going to be worth doing.

door_when.open_toast: The work-room door swings in on a room that smells of hot metal and cold stone.
